abstract: Ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm is a new meta-heuristic for hard combinational optimization problem. In order to resolve QoS multicast routing effectively and efficiently, this paper firstly describe QoS multicast routing model and ACO algorithm, then a new version of ACO algorithm based on pheromone local and global updating rule is proposed. Simulation results show that this algorithm can find optimal solution quickly and has a good scalability.

articleTitle: A fair admission control scheme for multimedia wireless network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: CAC (call admission control) scheme plays an important role in the QoS guarantee of wireless multimedia network. Lots of CAC schemes aim to satisfy QoS requirement and upgrade network utilization, but they ignore the fairness principle in network. Directly and simply using these schemes, it will appear the phenomenon of unbalance that the narrow band calls block the broad band calls. The common method used to resolve fair problem is resource reservation method, but it will decrease the network utilization. So, this paper proposes a novel fair call admission control scheme. Differing from resource reservation method, the new scheme introduces call hold control method to overcome unfair problem between narrow band calls and broad band calls. Numerical results show that the new scheme effectively improves network utilization and decreases CBP (call blocking probability) especially when the network carries heavy traffic load. Simulation results also show that the average waiting time of users is much less than their waiting time thresholds and users could receive the service in a short waiting time.

articleTitle: Sensors deployment in energy efficient wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the influence of correlated data from different sensors on the location of the sensors and the consumed energy of wireless sensor network are introduced, and the performance of a joint entropy encoding strategy which compresses the correlated data along routing is analyzed. During transmission, relay sensors jointly encode their own sampled data and the data received from upward sensors. The consumed energy of the network is minimized through optimally choosing the location of sensors. For the sake of prolonging network lifetime, a scheme to balance the consumed energy between different sensors is proposed, which combines the correlation between data and the amounts of data transmitted by different sensors, to make the transmitted energy consumed by different sensors tend to be uniform by adjusting the distance between sensors. The applications of the schemes in one-dimensional wireless sensor network are presented and the numerical results show that these schemes have excellent performance.

articleTitle: A hybrid ARQ scheme with constellation rearrangement and power adjustment
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: There are many parameters to be selected in the hybrid-ARQ (automatic repeat request) systems, e.g., transmission power, modulation format, bit-to-symbol mapping in the constellation and so on. In the retransmissions, different parameters or the combination of them could be selected to improve the performance. This paper proposes a new HARQ scheme, where the constellation mapping and the transmission power in the retransmissions differ with the new transmission. Compared to the conventional HARQ schemes, the proposed scheme can increase the throughput and decrease the average number of retransmissions and the power consumption.

articleTitle: Applications of mobile agent and digital watermarking technologies in mobile communication network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A digital watermark system based on mobile agent is designed in this paper, which can reduce the load of server and network during detecting digital watermark of multimedia on Internet. It effectively enables the technology of copyright protection of multimedia-digital watermark to be put into practice.

articleTitle: Throughput analysis of IEEE 802.11 DCF over correlated fading channel in MANET
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The throughput of 802.11 DCF over correlated fading channel in MANET are investigated in this paper. By obtaining the analytical representation of saturation throughput of 802.11 DCF over correlated fading channel, we get the impact of frame length and the mobile speed on throughput. Study shows the throughput decreases with the increase of mobile velocity and there exists an optimal frame length to maximize throughput under a certain velocity. Moreover, the optimal length is independent of the number of nodes.

articleTitle: Performance of a queuing model With Pareto input traffic for wireless network nodes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In the past few years, packet traffic from various sources - Ethernet, ISDN, CCSN and VBR video - has been shown to exhibit self-similarity and related properties of long range correlation. Recent research has shown that self-similar nature of traffic still exists in the traffic of wireless networks. Since Pareto process generates self-similar arrivals, we analyzed the queue behavior with Pareto interarrival and exponential service time distribution via phase-type (PH) distributions fitting technique and matrix geometric solution approach. Average queue length and loss probability were derived and verified via extensive simulations and the results can provide a practical insight into the buffer dimensioning and admission control as well as QoS providing for wireless network.

articleTitle: Relation between beamforming and diversity in feedback MIMO system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In mobile communication, frequency domain and time domain have been used adequately, then, space domain is an important domain to use. This paper studies feedback MIMO system, investigates the relation between beamforming and space diversity. In FDD regime, we use codebook known to both transmitter and receiver to decide either beamforming or space diversity to increase reliability. Both methods can guarantee full diversity order. Since MIMO system with two antennas at mobile station is applicable, we compare performances of beamforming and diversity, which shows that beamforming is better at low SNR and space diversity is better at high SNR on perfect channel estimation. When diversity order is four, their performances are not increased so fast as diversity order increases; therefore, there is a diminishing gain.

articleTitle: A waveform generate unit suitable for software defined HFSWR
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A new radio frequency waveform generate unit is presented for software-defined high frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR). Since HFSWR operates in congested band, to suppress interference and clutters, together obtain the optimal combined sequence of waveform parameters, the radar system should be designed based on software radio principle. In this paper we discuss a software defined HF radar system-OSMAR2003, and focus on design and implementation of waveform generate unit for it. The proposed waveform generation unit integrates a frequency synthesizer with low phase noise and high signal to noise rate and a re-configurable synchronization control unit. The design is started with examination of requirements of the waveform and then optimize architecture of the combination of the synthesizer technology to satisfy the system requirements. Followed is the FPGA (field programmable logic array) based synchro unit controlled by VXI-bus. The measurement shows that the transmitted signal can be synthesized quickly with phase noise less than -109 dBc/Hz at 1-kHz off carrier and spur suppression greater than 65 dBc, While the waveform parameters can be set by VXI-bus. The signal generate unit becomes an important part of the software defined HFSWR and field experiments provide the validity.

articleTitle: An approach to localized edge detection in SHM
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Structure health monitoring (SHM) is a driving force for extending capability of wireless sensor networks system. At the same time, structure monitoring brings new challenges to wireless sensor network. Localized edge detection is one of them. This paper presented an approach using image processing theory for edge detection in SHM.

articleTitle: A novel method of channel estimation for DRM system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A novel method of channel estimation adaptable to DRM system is proposed. According to the characterization of the OFDM parameter and pilot pattern defined in DRM standard [ETSI ES, 2003-04], channel estimation has to be done first in time and then in frequency direction. Linear interpolation filter is used in time direction, and windowed DFT channel estimation is used in frequency direction. Simulation results show this method has better performance with low computation complexity.

articleTitle: A power-saving routing algorithm based on ant algorithm in mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, a method of an improved ant algorithm called PSAA (power-saving ant algorithm) is proposed for ad hoc networks to prolong the life-time of ad hoc networks as long as possible. The battery remainder power and its variance of nodes in ad hoc networks are taken into account in PSAA. Variance of battery remainder power of nodes shows the equilibrium of every nodes power consumption partially. Leading in the mutation strategy that has a random small probability, PSAA can avoid getting into local optimal solutions. So the selected routing is more reasonable. Furthermore, PSAA sets hop constraint to provide QoS guarantee. Simulation shows PSAA is more efficient and robust than other power saving algorithms, especially when topology of networks changes rapidly. PSAA also has a longer lifetime.

articleTitle: Gene expression programming based on simulated annealing
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Gene expression programming (GEP) is a genotype/phenotype system that evolves computer programs of different sizes and shapes encoded in linear chromosomes of fixed length. However, the performance of basic GEP is highly dependent on the genetic operators' rate. In this work, we present a new algorithm called GEPSA that combines GEP and simulated annealing (SA), and GEPSA decreases the dependence on genetic operators' rate without impairing the performance of GEP. Three function finding problems, including a benchmark problem of prediction sunspots, are tested on GEPSA, results shows that importing simulated annealing can improve the performance of GEP.

articleTitle: The performance of STBC coded MIMO-OFDM system based on turbo product codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Space-time block codes (STBCs) are designed to obtain the full diversity gain. However, STBCs are not designed to achieve an additional coding gain. Therefore, STBCs need to be concatenated with an outer code which provides a significant coding gain. Turbo product codes (TPCs) are a kind of high-efficient coding scheme with low latency decoding, which do not suffer from an error floor associated with turbo codes. This article considers the concatenation of TPCs with STBCs and sets up coded MIMO-OFDM system to improve the reliability of the wireless communication systems. Finally, the paper presents simulating environment of experiment testing.

articleTitle: Inter-satellite link design for the LEO/MEO two-layered satellite network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Inter-satellite link (ISL) design is an important part of the design for satellite networks. Dynamic characteristic of ISLs affects the network performance. We propose an ISL link stability model in this paper. Based on the stability model, a link design scheme for satellite networks is presented. The scheme includes static and dynamic link design phases where static and dynamic types of ISLs are treated respectively. Finally the performance of ISL design scheme is evaluated in a LEO/MEO two-layered satellite network. The simulation results shows that the link design scheme is applicable to requirement of diverse services.

articleTitle: Voice activity detection algorithm improvement in adaptive multi-rate speech coding of 3GPP
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Aimed at the voice activity detection algorithm in adaptive multi-rate speech coding scheme of 3GPP, a novel and accurate speech activity detection algorithm was developed in this article. The new algorithm was simpler than original in performance and would bring the effect as good as the old one, especially superior to former algorithm in estimation of voice tail.

articleTitle: A power-saving protocol for ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: To extend the usage scope of an 802.11DCF based wireless LAN power-saving protocol 802.11PS to a multi-hop mobile environment, a modified protocol called 802.11NPS is proposed. It uses a packet-driven dynamic switching-off mechanism on the wireless network interface card to save power. By delaying the switching-off operations for a certain period of time after nodes receiving unrelated control packets, 802.11NPS can support the upper layer routing protocol excellently and thus can be used in multi-hop ad hoc networks. It also can be used in fully connected networks. By using a more accurate power-consumption model, the performance of 802.11NPS is studied through simulation. Results show that in a WLAN environment, 802.11NPS can save power by more than 60% as compared with 802.11DCF; while in a multi-hop mobile environment, 802.11NPS can save power by 18%. At the meanwhile, its delay performance is better than that of 802.11DCF and the throughput is still similar.

articleTitle: Joint order and channel estimation with evolutionary algorithm
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The classic adaptive channel estimation algorithms exhibit high dependence on the prior knowledge of channel order. In this paper, a joint order and channel estimation algorithm is proposed. By exploiting the excellent global optimization performance of the evolutionary algorithm, the channel order and channel impulse response are evolved at the same time with the MSE as fitness function. The experimental results on simulated channel show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the traditional LMS estimation approach in initial convergence rate as well as the tolerance upon order underestimation.

articleTitle: The low complexity deterministic SMC detection algorithm for MIMO system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents a low complexity deterministic sequential Monte Carlo (DSMC) detection scheme, called multi-level mapping DSMC detector, for high-order QAM constellations. The new scheme utilizes the property of QAM constellation and performs the sequence weight calculation in steps of two bits, which reduces the complexity. Being soft-input soft-output in nature, the multi-level mapping DSMC detector can be employed as the first-stage demodulator in a turbo receiver in coded MIMO systems. As a suboptimum detector with complexity linear in the number of transmit antennas, the multilevel mapping DSMC detector provides performance practically identical with that of the basic DSMC detector, and reduces the complexity from exponential in the modulation coefficient to linear with the modulation coefficient. Computer simulation for the uncoded MIMO system in the flat fading channel and the coded MIMO-OFDM turbo receiver system in the frequency selective multi-path fading channel proves the performance.

articleTitle: An improvement fast INTER mode selection for H.264 joint with spatio-temporal correlation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Considering the much computational complexity of selecting inter macroblock coding mode for H.264, an improved fast mode decision is proposed in this paper by exploiting the features in spatio-temporal domain. Simulations show that the proposed algorithm reduces the encoding time by 89.94% on average without consideration performance degradation.

articleTitle: An novel timing acquisition algorithm for OFDM systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper a novel and efficient symbol timing estimation algorithm is proposed for OFDM systems. This algorithm utilizes inherent correlation property of two segments of information sequence to carry out accurate symbol timing estimation. The studying results show that the algorithm can complete timing acquisition under large frequency offset and low SNR accurately. Furthermore it is no need of special training symbol, so the system's transmission efficiency is increased largely.

articleTitle: Accurate geometrical analysis of sector dwell time distribution
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we present accurate evaluation of sector dwell time distribution based on geometric analysis methods. Considering the nature geometric characteristic of the deployed sector pattern, and the distribution of the mobiles' position and moving direction in the given sector, we derive the accurate formulas of the probability density function of sector cell dwell time. Some numerical results are also presented for illustration.

articleTitle: Analyze of the blind equalization based on second-order statistics of the over-sampling signal
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The blind channel equalization based on second-order statistics of the over-sampling signal can identify nonminimum phase multipath channels, it has good convergence properties, needs less computation and can achieve equalization with fewer symbols than most techniques based only on higher-order statistics. The paper not only expounds the channel model and the over-sampling signal's cyclostationarity, but also does some simulations to analyse the performance of the blind equalization method as the sampling rate changes.

articleTitle: Chart design of iterative decoding
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Two simple and efficient charts for iterative decoding are proposed, called output mutual information chart with defined iterative degree (DID Chart) and near optimum output mutual information chart (NOMI Chart). Compared with BER performance curve, they show the iterative performance on the whole signal-to-noise ratio range with reduced computation complexity. The concepts are illustrated for bit-interleaved coded modulation with iterative decoding (BICM-ID). Some possible usages are also presented.

articleTitle: Proportional gradient satisfaction strategy in wireless scheduling
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Traditional scheduling strategies base their goals on maximizing the total system throughput. However, in recent research, the maximized total throughput does not necessarily represent the optimal system resource allocation. In this paper, we propose the proportional gradient satisfaction strategy (PGSS), which adds user satisfaction value to the existing scheduling criteria. PGSS schedules bandwidth in proportion to the temporal satisfaction gradient rather than original bandwidths used in traditional scheduling strategies. Moreover, PGSS substitutes user satisfaction value with its gradient to simplify the nonlinear problem of satisfaction value, traditionally solved by intelligence algorithms, in order to reduce the algorithm complexity to make PGSS practical to implement in a base station. Simulation shows that compared with proportional compensation algorithm, PGSS promotes the system aggregated satisfaction value and still guarantees the maximized system throughout.

articleTitle: Design and simulations of underwater acoustic communication receiver without PLL
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A kind of receiver is designed for underwater acoustic communications to cope with the combined limitations of time-varying multipath and phase instabilities of the underwater channel. After quadrature demodulation and mathematical transform, the carrier phase error can be eliminated. As phase-locked loop (PLL) is not needed to track the carrier phase shift during equalization, the computational complexity can be reduced. Simulations on two different types of multipath and phase shift channels show that good performance can be achieved for the simple channel model, while satisfactory results can be obtained through multichannel diversity combining for the other channel.

articleTitle: Low complexity adaptive MIMO-OFDM system for transmission under correlated frequency-selective channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Existing works on MIMO systems have been restricted to either uncorrelated frequency-selective channels or correlated non frequency-selective channels. Practical MIMO systems however, suffers from the effects of frequency selectivity and channel correlation due to the high transmission rate and proximity of the transmit antennas. This paper presents a low complexity adaptive MIMO-OFDM system. The system exploits the time, frequency and spatial dimensions to provide high data rate and robust signal transmission in frequency selective channels with varying correlation levels. Compared to existing MIMO-OFDM systems, the proposed system provides up to 2-3 dB gains under low channel correlations and more than 5 dB gains in highly correlated channel.

articleTitle: A study on the pieces on seed for mobile peer-to-peer file sharing applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Piece selection is one of fundamental operations for mobile P2P file sharing applications, to some extent, it would affect the integrity of file what users obtain. Having investigated the feature of piece selection algorithm of BitTorrent carefully, a new piece selection algorithm based on seed control is presented in this paper. Comparing with the piece selection algorithm of BitTorrent, the proposed one(PSASC) requires seed to control the piece selection in order to avoid its repetition. The-set-covering problem and greedy approximation algorithm are utilized to analyze time complexities of piece selection algorithm of BitTorrent and PSASC, and the simulation is given. Results indicate that the time complexity of PSASC outperforms that of BitTorrent, and shorten the time that all pieces on seed are allocated into mobile P2P network. Finally, based on PSASC, the relation between the n pieces on seed and the mean time T~ that each piece has been downloaded is obtained by M/M/1/m/m queuing model.

articleTitle: Analysis of SDMA PCT-II traffic for duplicate first case - a theoretical approach
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In any wireless communication main goal is to maximize carried traffic within limited spectrum or channel. In space division multiple access (SDMA) same beam could be repeated in different direction hence same logical channel can support multiple users simultaneously. This access technique is equally applicable in mobile cellular network, wireless local loop and satellite communications to enhance carried traffic. This paper deals with theoretical analysis of a SDMA traffic for a wireless network in generalized form with provision of primary and secondary beam for limited user case of course duplicate first allocation technique is considered.

articleTitle: The design of high precision and low power communication signal source based on AD9954
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The paper introduces the technology of the direct digital frequency synthesis and the structure and functions and features of AD9954 in detail. A SCM, AT89c51, controls the read-in of program words of AD9954 and the SCM is connected to PC by the communication interface RS-232. Accordingly we can get a high precision and low power communication signal source. And the signal working process is controlled by PC. It is commendably applied to the portable responder of the high frequency ground wave radar.

articleTitle: Blind asynchronous multiuser detection in impulsive CDMA channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper we propose a new method in multiuser detection for asynchronous CDMA channel in which we use a series of training bits to obtain the characteristics of the channel. Each of the samples of a spreaded bit experiences different noise parameters due to the periodic nature of signature wave forms. As a result, one must calculate noise probability density function (pdf) for each bit position which is done here through the train phase. After finishing the train phase, the process of detecting bits is almost real time. As we estimate the channel parameters, this method can be assumed a blind one.

articleTitle: On the capacity of quasi orthogonal space-time block codes for MIMO systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: It is well known that the Alamouti scheme with two transmit antennas and one receive antennas is the only capacity-achieving complex orthogonal space-time block code (OSTBC). The rate of complex OSTBC for systems with more than two transmit antennas is always less than 1. Recently, a quasi orthogonal space-time block code (QSTBC) with four transmit antennas and one receive antenna was proposed, which has the ability to approach the capacity, although at the price of sacrificing part of the diversity gain. In this paper, we analyze the capacity of QSTBC with four transmit antennas and arbitrary number of receive antennas. We show that the portion of the capacity that the QSTBC can achieve decreases with the number of receive antennas, and the (4,1) configuration is the only capacity-approaching case. In the high signal-to-noise ratio regime, we calculate the limit portion of capacity of QSTBC, and find that it is fixed to 1/4 when the number of receive antennas is no less than four. Numerical simulations verify our conclusions.

articleTitle: A FOA-based error resiliency scheme for video transmission over unreliable channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Traditional error control schemes considered videos as low-level bit streams, ignoring the underlying visual content. When viewing one video sequence, people often pay more attention to some specific visual object than others. This "focusing effect" is what we called 'focus of attention' (FOA). If video content is taken into considerations during error resilience process, the network resource can be utilized efficiently, and salient regions which attract attention can be protected hierarchically. As a result, the reconstructed video can satisfy the user's perception demand maximally. The FOA-based error resiliency schemes proposed in this paper divide the video content into three hierarchies according to human's attention sequence, then associating with representative error resiliency model. As a result, the most valuable information is achieved at the minim cost.

articleTitle: A gatekeeper-based NAT traversal method for media transport in H.323 network system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: H.323 has application to a variety of network media, including local area networks, enterprise networks, Internet and wireless networks. But NAT (network address translation) traversal problem is baffling H.323 communication due to complex network situations and flaws of protocol. The existing traversal methods are not suitable for all network situations. They often require upgrading or adding other deceives and protocols to support call procedure. In this paper, A NAT traversal method based on gatekeeper (GK) for media transport is proposed. This scheme only needs a gatekeeper server, which is able to route call. This resolving method is also very easy to implement without changing network situations. And it is very available for communications with many NAT deceives in applications. The mechanism may be used as the short-term solution for the NAT traversal problem in H.323 system.

articleTitle: Turbo codes with non-primitive component codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Unlike previous work on turbo codes in which both the feedback and generator polynomials used in the component codes are limited to primitive polynomials, in this paper a comparison of primitive and non-primitive feedback and generator polynomials is given. Simulation results over the AWGN channel show that non-primitive polynomials can achieve better performance at very low SNR. On this basis we comment on the conditions under which non-primitive turbo-codes may give better results than those based on primitive polynomials.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of CDMA signals and the realization utilizing TMS320
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, an effective DOA estimation algorithm, element-wise division operation, is presented for DS-CDMA system under multi-user environment. Because the algorithm requires neither complex eigenvalue decomposition operations nor source number estimation, the algorithm can be realized timely utilizing DSP device TMS320, and the circuit structure and flow chart is presented.

articleTitle: Rejection of narrowband interference in DS-SS systems employing decision feedback filters
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The performance of direct-sequence spread spectrum systems in the present of narrowband interference rejection is studied employing decision feedback filters. Closed-form analytical expressions for the system's performance are derived. Both analysis results and numerical simulation results show that DF filters outperform linear prediction filters by comparison.

articleTitle: The key research on integrating wireless sensor network with grid
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: It is a wonderful grope for integrating wireless sensor network which acts as an infrastructure of sensing environment around with open grid computing. The combination of the two systems poses many challengers. This paper has analyzed the key characters of the connecting platform for integrating sensor network with grid. We also designed and developed such a connecting platform which supports communication & collaboration between sensor network and grid. The advantage of the connecting platform is that it is based on Web service resource framework, with the ability of integrating multiple sensor networks with grid; also it supports interoperability among multiple sensor networks. The simulation results show that the notification mechanism which is restricted by the running resource is the key factor for getting sensor data successfully.

articleTitle: A novel link adaptation strategy combining transmit diversity and spatial multiplexing in space over time-varying channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: For multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems the link adaptation (LA) can significantly increase the system throughput. In the existing scheme of spatial multiplexing (SM), the link adaptation has been done by adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) on every sub-channel with QoS limit. However, the throughput loss occurs at lower SNR because the SM has no transmit diversity (TD). In this paper a novel LA strategy is proposed to solve the problem mentioned above by combining TD and SM over space. This combining scheme is adaptively to find the optimal spatial group scheme of the transmit antennas based on the derived post detection SNR and to do SM with them, which may use space-time block codes (STBC) with the QoS limit. The simulation results show that, with low complexity, this method can outperform the LA algorithm in conventional multiplexing scheme in the throughput performance and obtain higher transmit power utilization and decrease the number of invalid antennas.

articleTitle: Performance of differential quasi-orthogonal space-time block coded cellular system in the presence of interference
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a simple differential quasi-orthogonal space-time block code, which can offer full rate and full diversity. At the transmitter end, we divide the codes into sub-coding blocks, and combine the sub-coding blocks into one at the receiver to employ differential decoding by channel power estimation instead of decoding each sub-coding block at first hand. Our general approach can be extended to the recent proposed quasi-orthogonal codes with full rate and half diversity. Moreover, this scheme is not limited to PSK constellations but can also utilize QAM constellations, so that additional coding gain can be obtained. We first examine our work in an individual link with fixed position without the presence of co-channel interference. Then, we investigate the performance in MIMO cellular systems.

articleTitle: Implementation of the trusted computing in commercial cryptogram based on embedded system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Trusted computing is an important aspect of information security. The current algorithms of commercial cryptogram based on software in many fields often are not trusted. This paper proposes a new approach based on embedded system to implement the algorithms of commercial cryptogram, which can overcome the shortage of algorithm based on software, such as less security and low speed. And the prototype of the approach is also implemented in this paper, which contains FPGA and embedded system as a system on chip (SOC).

articleTitle: An improved unequal error protection turbo codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The principle of turbo codes has been analyzed in this paper, and a new unequal error protection turbo codes by designing a new puncturing scheme are proposed. The experiment results proved that under the condition of not increasing the system complexity when the BER is lower than 10/sup -4/, the UEP turbo codes achieve a coding gain over the EEP codes of about 0.6 dB on the AWGN channel, effectively realizing the protection of the important information in the encoded signal.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of high-availability routing software
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: With the explosion in the use of Internet, there is an obvious trend that critical applications based on IP network (E-transaction, etc.) are increasing dramatically. Therefore, it is required to build high performance routers (HPRs) with high availability (HA). Though researches on HA router hardware are fairly mature, investigations on HA routing software are still on-going. This paper systematically presents possible implementation approaches on HA routing software and classifies them into three catalogs: protocol extension, state synchronization and packet duplication. This paper innovatively models and analyzes these HA routing software schemes in continuous-time Markov chains (CTMC). Based on the modeling, this paper also introduces numerical results and evaluates these different HA approaches.

articleTitle: On the capacity region of wireless relay networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Network capacity is a key characteristic to evaluate the performance of wireless networks. The capacity of wireless ad hoc network that is a rising network model has been discussed widely. The goal of this paper is to study about the capacity of wireless relay network. We assume that at most n/sub s/ source nodes transmitting signal simultaneously in the network and derive the upper and lower bound on the capacity of this kind network model. Finally, the capacity region of wireless relay network by simulations in the idealized condition is given.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of free space optical communication system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new channel model of free space optical communication system. The physics meaning of this model is very clear, and its format is very simple. Mathematic results show that multiple beams are a very effective way for intensity fluctuation reduction induced by turbulence, thus reduce the bit-error-rate of the system.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of LDPC codes with 16QAM in nonlinear channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper gives the performance evaluation of LDPC codes with three 16QAM constellations under a nonlinear channel. Simulation results show that LDPC codes with rectangular 16QAM has the best BER performance among the three constellations regarded under linear channel, while the rectangular 16QAM and star (8,8) constellation have the best performance in nonlinear channel.

articleTitle: Virtual destination based geographic routing in ad hoc mobile networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A new algorithm is proposed to forward packet when greedy forwarding fails. The concept of virtual destination is introduced and virtual destination based geographic routing protocol is brought forth. The protocol only uses greedy scheme which is different from existing geographic routing protocols which use greedy scheme and face algorithm. We evaluate our proposed scheme by random connected unit graph. The results show that our routing protocol is superior to the greedy perimeter stateless routing (GPSR) in term of average number of hops in connected ad hoc networks.

articleTitle: A novel cross-layer routing scheme of ad hoc networks with multi-rate mechanism
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A novel cross-layer routing technique was proposed for ad hoc networks with multi-rate mechanism based on node monitoring information. Combining SNR measure on physical layer and delay estimate on MAC layer, we propose a routing metric which selects the route with wide bandwidth, lower delay and less congestion. The routing technique is shown to improve performance of ad hoc network significantly.

articleTitle: Influence of space-time correlation and Rician fast fading on performance of MIMO system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: MIMO technology is effective to deal with wireless channel fading and support reliable, high-data-rate transmission. While the wireless system must cope with the space-time correlation and fast Rician fading in MIMO system. In this paper, we investigate the influence of space-time correlation and Rician fast fading on the performance of MIMO system. We derive the upper bound of the average pairwise error probability in space-time correlation Rician fast fading channels. Ultimately, we compare the influence of different channel characters on the performance of system.

articleTitle: K nearest neighbors search for the trajectory of moving object
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of finding the K nearest neighbors for the trajectory of moving object in the context where the dataset is static and stored in an R-tree. By converted into discovering the K nearest neighbors of the line segment, this kind of query is simplified. Several distance functions between MBRs and line segments are defined and used to prune search space and minimize the pruning distance. Based on branch-and-bound technique and proposed pruning, updating and visiting heuristics, recursive depth-first and heap-based best-first algorithms are presented. An extensive study based on experiments performed with synthetic dataset shows that best-first algorithm outperforms the depth-first algorithm.

articleTitle: High power amplifier or site power sharing: comparison of two low cost solutions to boost UMTS downlink capacity
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The expected increase of asymmetric traffic in wireless 3G networks is likely to generate capacity limitations in down link (DL). In this paper we investigate and compare two DL capacity enhancement techniques alternative to densification or multi-carrier, viz. the use of 40 W power amplifiers, and the use of site power sharing, i.e. the possibility for one sector to use the available power from power amplifiers of other co-sited sectors. Using a dynamic simulator on a real urban network, we show that both solutions allow to improve the DL capacity of the network. Very interestingly we show that for admission and upholding probabilities greater than 85%, both methods are almost equivalent. They should hence be compared according to their implementation and maintenance costs.

articleTitle: An improved decoding algorithm of low-density parity-check codes
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, the decoding algorithm of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is analyzed, and a new decoding algorithm based on the belief propagation (BP) algorithm to eliminate the influence of cycles in the factor graph is proposed. In the traditional BP algorithm, the cycles of factor graph sends message back to its source, and this decreases the decoding performance. The new algorithm records each cycle's path and length of each node, and cuts off the path by which message is propagated when the message comes back. It can advance the decoding performance by protect the message of good quality be propagated as widely as possible. Our results of simulation show that the performance of new algorithm is not worse than that of traditional BP algorithm in the low SNR channel and the new algorithm significantly outperform traditional BP algorithm in good channel condition.

articleTitle: MIMO wireless systems: overcoming the problems of convenience
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper we consider the fundamental advantage of wireless communication - its convenience - and the inevitable problems of spatial dispersion that this gives rise to. We show that MIMO systems, and especially adaptive MIMO systems, can overcome a number of these disadvantages by exploiting the spatial dimension. Especially we note that an adaptive MIMO system can combine the capacity/diversity advantages of MIMO with the benefits of 'smart antenna' systems in a wireless network.

articleTitle: Bridge nodes based secure OLSR
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The existing secure routing protocols for ad hoc network are mainly based on bi-directional and symmetrical links, however, because of the special digital signals transmission equipments, which have different physical characteristic such as power range, there are many asymmetrical links in true wireless networks, so the successful authentication ratio is limited, even they can't work in some extreme circumstance. This paper proposes a bridge nodes based secure link state routing scheme-BSOLSR to solve the asymmetrical link problem. The simulation presents that the successful authentication ratio is enhanced and the average length of routing paths is shorter than that of SOLSR, which is important to the communication efficiency and networks performance.

articleTitle: Antenna subset selection algorithm based on sub-optimal sorting for MIMO systems with V-BLAST
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper discussed the problem of antenna subset selection in multiple-input multiple-output systems. Based on suboptimal sorting, we obtained the straightforward performance analysis with QR decomposition, and proposed a transmit antenna subset selection algorithm that is applicable for V-BLAST systems with ordered successive interference cancellation (OSIC) detection. Unlike most of the existing works, this criterion takes into account the impacts of ordering and cancellation. Simulations had shown that the proposed strategy achieves near-optimal outage capacity and outperforms the existing incremental selection and the norm-based algorithms in performance with reasonable complexity.

articleTitle: A distributed grouping algorithm for grid resources based on grey relational analysis
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we present the concepts of representation and quantification of market-based resources allocation in grid context, and then propose a distributed grouping algorithm based on grey relational analysis for resources grouping. The algorithm classifies grid resources into multiple groups by the measurement of grey relational degree between reference resource and comparing resource. At last, an example is given and the result indicates this proposed algorithm is effective for grid resources grouping and adaptive to grouped-resource price adjustment in the grid environment with economic mechanism.

articleTitle: A novel joint ML and DFE scheme for V-BLAST system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The use of multiple antennas at the transmitter and receiver results in enormous capacity increase. However, the performance of many current space-time architectures like Vertical Bell Laboratories Layered Space-Time (V-BLAST) is depend on the first sub-channel decoding's performance. In this paper, we present a novel detection algorithm, which joint ML and DFE scheme for the V-BLAST system. It can improve the V-BLAST system's performance by add ML modification module after the conventional detection scheme. It can also get the tradeoff between complexity and performance. Simulation result shows that the performance of the proposed scheme is better than that of conventional method.

articleTitle: A new bit-allocating algorithm for adaptive OFDM transmission system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper studies the bit loading algorithm for adaptive OFDM transmission system, and proposes an improved scheme called shifting-threshold algorithm. Using computer simulations, we show that the OFDM system employing the shifting threshold algorithm can enhance bit rate. On BER performance, the shifting threshold algorithm is better than fixed threshold algorithm.

articleTitle: A security enhanced AODV routing protocol based on the credence mechanism
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Ad hoc networks are characterized by open medium, dynamic topology, distributed cooperation and constrained capability. These characteristics set more challenges for security. Routing security is the most important factor in the security of the entire network. However, few of current routing protocols have the consideration about the security problems. This paper analyzes the potential insecurity factors in the AODV protocol. A security routing protocol based on the credence model is proposed, which can react quickly when some malicious behaviors in the network are detected and effectively protects the network from kinds of attacks and guarantees the security of ad hoc networks.

articleTitle: Ultra wideband frequency spectrum and multipath channel model
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The next generation mobile communication 4G will support high data transmission rate and high frequency efficiency. In order to satisfy the future requirements of fixed broadband wireless access systems, technical renovation on the physical layer and control layer is demanded and UWB is one of the most competitive technologies in future wireless communication systems. The paper discusses UWB frequency spectrum, modulation and MA technologies of UWB, and then emphatically analyzes multipath channel model of UWB proposed by IEEE 802.15. SG3a. Based on the research of UWB frequency spectrum and key technology, the results suggest that the new multipath channel model needs to be further modified.

articleTitle: Enhancing processing gain of UWB systems with NBI by signal parameters selection
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper presents the method for the signal parameters selection to improve the processing gain (PG) of the single-user TH ultra-wideband (UWB) systems. The signal parameters provided by this method are independent of TH codes. First, the UWB system models are introduced. The UWB system operates in the multipath channel with NBI, and employs binary pulse amplitude modulation. Next, the processing gain is derived. Then, the method is given. At last, the effectiveness of this method is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Behavior and performance improvement of TCP Vegas in LEO satellite networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: TCP Vegas is supportive to space communication. However, the performance degrades when it is used in LEO satellite networks. The handover and rerouting issues in LEO satellite networks cause path change and abrupt delay variance. The congestion window size should be increased when delay increases due to path change, but TCP Vegas reduces the window size by mistake, and the throughput degrades. In this paper, the behavior of TCP Vegas in LEO satellite network is studied. A method is proposed for correctly adjusting the congestion window when the path changes. Simulation results show that the method is validity and the performance of TCP Vegas is improved.

articleTitle: Channel adaptive resources management in wireless mobile computing systems: issues and new algorithms
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In a wireless mobile computing system such as ad hoc network or sensor network, it is very difficult to manage resources - the precious bandwidth shared by the mobile terminals and the energy in each mobile terminal - in an efficient manner, due to the lack of network infrastructure support. The difficulties are aggravated by the fact that the wireless link is highly unreliable with high-error rate and bursty errors, and thus, is a CSI (channel state information) dependent time-varying function. In this paper, we consider two important issues in mobile computing systems - routing in wireless ad hoc network and energy management in sensor network. We argue that the time-varying property of the wireless link can have a great influence on these two issues, and propose two schemes - channel adaptive routing in ad hoc network and channel adaptive energy management in sensor network under such CSI fluctuating environment. As indicated in our numerical studies, our proposed schemes outperform other algorithms without channel adaptation in that higher network throughput and energy efficiency are achieved in their respective application scenarios.

articleTitle: Target detection in first-order regions by bistatic radar
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper deals with first-order-region detection of target by bistatic system, which is a delicate problem for radar developers. A new bistatic model was presented, and the model-based method was developed to eliminate blind-speed zones. With analyzing the bistatic model geometry, by trigonometric cosine law, slave-radar data was utilized to restore target information if main-radar first-order sea echoes smeared the ship target. To get target signal from the slave radar, the ship target was firstly located in the slave radar roughly according to its last position in the main radar. Then for the candidate ship, the agreement of azimuth, distance and radial velocity between array-measured results and equation-solved values was used as acceptance criterion. The method shows good performance on the data recorded by ocean state measurement and analysis radar, a bistatic system manufactured in 2003 (OSMAR2003).

articleTitle: Improving the spectral efficiency of multiuser OFDM system with V/spl I.bar/BLAST architecture by adaptive resource allocation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of adaptive resource allocation in the downlink of multiuser OFDM systems with V/spl I.bar/BLAST architecture. In order to get a high spectral efficiency even in low SNR, we propose a novel low-complexity adaptive subchannel-bit allocation and power reallocation algorithm. The algorithm considers the users' quality of service (QoS) requirements. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm performs almost as well as the optimal solution. Moreover, higher spectral efficiency is achieved for larger number of users due to the multiuser diversity and the power reallocation is used in low SNR field.

articleTitle: Simulation of indoor ultra wideband propagation channel modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: UWB (ultra wideband) propagation channel modeling is very important for UWB communication system designing and its performance optimization. The split-field PML (perfectly matched layer) and unsplit-field PML were combined respectively with PSTD (pseudospectral time-domain) method to model 2-D (two dimensional) and 3-D indoor UWB propagation. The attenuation factor algorithm was applied to simulate realistic UWB propagation under 2-D environment. Channel characteristics were studied and the accuracy and efficiency of their modeling were also analyzed. Numerical simulations have indicated that the split-field and unsplit-field PML combined PSTD methods have the same accuracy while the consumed computer memory by unsplit method has been reduced to nearly one half of that by split method. Some resultant channel characteristics can be observable from the measurement results.

articleTitle: An active network based hierarchical mobile Internet protocol version 6 framework
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The mobile Internet protocol version 6 (MIPv6), based on IPv6, will be widely used in the next generation wireless network. The latency of the handover is one of the most important parameters in evaluating MIPv6. At present, the popular wireless handover technologies include the fast mobile Internet protocol version 6 (FMIPv6) and the hierarchical mobile IPv6 (HMIPv6) invented by IETF and the active network invented by DARPA. In this paper, we propose a new strategy of the wireless handover in MIPv6, which is based on the HMIPv6 and the active network. The strategy will optimize the handover process during MN's roaming. In the network simulator (NS-2), we set up a simulation scenario. We compare the handover performance of the network architecture using our strategy with that of HMIPv6 and prove that our strategy has better performance.

articleTitle: Expanded subspace approaches for multiuser detection for CDMA multipath frequency selective fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Multiuser detection for direct-sequence code-division multiple-access (DS/CDMA) multipath frequency-selective fading channels with intersymbol interference (ISI) is considered. The concept of expanded signal subspace is introduced to characterize the unique property of the CDMA systems in multipath channels. By fully exploiting the structure of the expanded signal subspace, novel expanded approaches are developed to jointly suppress ISI and multiple access interference (MAI). Simulations have verified that the proposed detectors are immune to MAI and ISI and are near-far resistant, significantly outperforming the conventional multiuser detectors.

articleTitle: Optimal eigen-beamforming combined with orthogonal STBC and TCM in correlation fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper develops a novel system which combines the two dimensional (2D) eigen-beamforming (EBF) with orthogonal space-time block code (O-STBC) and trellis coded modulation (TCM) for transmit correlation fading channels. The corresponding statistic error event probability analytical expressions, power load algorithms and TCM design criteria are achieved respectively for two cases: with or without interleaver. The former achieves build-in-time diversity besides beamforming diversity and code gain from product-sum distance, and which requires channel correlations to keep constant over the interleaving length. The latter obtains beamforming diversity and code gain from free distance. The power allocation algorithms show a new feature that relates to code distance other than minimum Euclidian distance among constellation points, which can lows the threshold of achieving beamforming diversity. The conventional ID beamforming is proved to be a special case. Furthermore, the analysis and simulation results show the proposed system can offer good performance with low decode complexity and has no space-time code rate lost with random number of transmit antennas.

articleTitle: A segment encryption and transmission scheme for wireless sensor network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Some wireless sensor networks (WSNs) must transmit the data to users securely and quickly. The sensor nodes just have limited computation, communication and storage capabilities. Moreover adversary can easily eavesdrop in the process of message transmission, the data should be protected through encryption. In this paper, we present a new data encryption scheme for the transmission, which uses the lightweight cryptography and lets several sensor nodes to encrypt and transmit data cooperatively, thus it can lighten the load of single sensor node, ensure the communication security, provide good load balancing and a higher lifetime of the network.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a novel bit synchronization method in short-wave frequency hopping communication networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A novel bit synchronization method based on time-slot is proposed in this paper according to the characteristic of frequency hopping (FH) signal. Software design and implementation of the method on TMS320C54x DSP is further discussed. The simulation results show that the method could achieve a simple implementation and short synchronization time, and could solve the problems of bit synchronization in short-wave FH communication networks.

articleTitle: Application of a genetic algorithm to Hopfield network multi-user detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this study, a hybrid approach that employs Hopfield network and a genetic algorithm for multi-user detection problem in code division multiple access system is proposed. The hybrid detection makes use of the global convergence advantage of the genetic algorithm to deal with the output of the Hopfield network detection. So the novel detection will not converge on the minimum of local energy function as the Hopfield network detection. And the computer simulation results show that this detection has good performance both in multiple-access interference resistance and near-far effect resistance.

articleTitle: RichUl : A new U1 component library based on J2ME
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: With the popularity of mobile phone, the function of the mobile phone has extended from communication tool to other areas, such as amusement, game, Web browsing, and so on. Most of the mobile manufactures have provided some toolkits in their products for developing such kinds of tools. However, different toolkits provided by different mobile phone manufacturers are quite different, mainly on screen size, screen color, way of key-press responsing and unicode character displaying, etc. One must develop the software for particular kind of mobile phones, and it is not easy to transplant the software from one kind of mobile phones to another kind, which bothers the developers quite well. To solve above problems, we have developed a wireless component library, RichUI. By using RichUI, developers can only concentrate on the development of business function without considering the details of different toolkit implementations, and the software developed based on RichUI can be used in different kinds of mobile phones.

articleTitle: Multistage quasi-orthogonal minimum output energy multiuser detector analysis for turbo coded CDMA systems in frequency-selective fading
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The paper presents the performance analysis of the multistage quasi-orthogonal minimum output energy (QOMOE) detector for a turbo coded synchronous CDMA systems in frequency selective fading environment. The QOMOE detector minimizes the output variance with respect to the component equivalent to the quasi-orthogonal component to the desired user's signature waveform, then the solution is the linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) transformation. The QOMOE receiver employs maximal-ratio combiner (MRC) for detecting the desired user. A comparison is made among multistage detectors, namely; QOMOE-MRC, matched filter (MF-MRC), decorrelator-MRC, LMMSE-MRC and blind adaptive-MRC receivers, in a frequency selective fading channel. Analysis and simulation results show that the multistage QOMOE-MRC can obtain better performance than that of other considered detectors.

articleTitle: Reliable and energy-efficient data collection modelling in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: One of the major challenges in data-gathering wireless sensor networks (WSNs) is to achieve the reliable and energy-efficient data collection. In this paper, we investigate using the spatial correlation of sensor observations to model information accuracy and power consumption in WSNs. Both our analysis and simulation results show that the pre-defined information accuracy can be achieved with only a limited number of sensors jointly sensing the same event. Hence, lots of power can be saved to prolong the network lifetime.

articleTitle: An efficient energy distribution scheme in sensor networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Energy distribution is an important issue in sensor networks. Most solutions have not efficiently combined load balancing and energy awareness. This paper firstly proves that the maximum energy consumption will happen around the sink node on the basis of the critical analysis. An efficient energy-aware load-balancing delivery scheme is proposed. It lets the sink node take the responsibility to manage a core set in which the nodes are one hop to the sink. The nodes in the core set will transmit the traffic according to decisive energy ratio (DER) with an efficient energy distribution way. The simulations show the proposed scheme is very efficient and simple to be implemented.

articleTitle: A novel energy-efficient algorithm in weight-different ad hoc wireless network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: We propose several novel localized algorithms to construct energy efficient routing structures for unhomogeneous wireless ad hoc networks, where some nodes have more weight than other nodes. And, we have also considered the functions of networks to fulfil. Our main aim is to make the network perform more functions in longer period.

articleTitle: Optimization of irregular LDPC codes on Rician channel
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: For irregular LDPC codes,the density evolution method can track the messages to find out the noise threshold, enabling optimization of the degree distribution. A new optimized scheme for irregular LDPC codes is proposed in this paper, which is combining Zhengya He's modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm with discrete density evolution (DDE) for the offset BP-based decoding algorithm. Several optimized degree distribution pairs and corresponding threshold of LDPC codes over Rician channel were given using the proposed scheme. The performance of the optimized LDPC codes was also analyzed. Simulation results shows that the proposed scheme is effective.

articleTitle: An approach of intelligent optimization system for mobile communication networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, a new intelligent optimization system based on history inversion prediction databases and data mining techniques for mobile communication networks is presented. In this system, intelligent optimization techniques are realized based on intelligent drive test. With the support of these techniques, network engineers are able to get the real-time analyzing results of mobile networks' working state, and then adjust the plan of the drive test and the strategy of network optimization to resolve problems existing in mobile communication networks in time. This system provides a more efficient method for the network engineers to analyze and manage the wireless networks, which can avoid the blindness, reduce workloads of network engineers and improve the effect and efficiency of network optimization.

articleTitle: Load forecasting method with feedback chaos item
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: To describe the non-linear relation of load time series, a improved centroid method with non-liner feedback chaos item is presented. The method is realized by a fuzzy neural networks model which is not entirely linked. The defuzzification of the model adopts centroid method. In order to extend the scope of weight acting, the non-linear feedback item of weight value is employed to form chaos learning algorithm, which can make the system find the global minimal point or its approximation quickly and enhance the stability of the model. The simulation results show preferable forecasting capability of the model.

articleTitle: Comparison of two channel estimation methods
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The pilot-assisted channel estimation method was studied in time-division multiplexing Rayleigh fading channel. Known time-multiplexed pilot symbols were transmitted periodically and their channel coefficients were estimated using ML estimation method. An improved channel estimation method employing Chebyshev polynomials as interpolation polynomial is introduced for downlink coherent receiver in LASMAX mobile environment in place of linear interpolation. The performance is compared with linear interpolation with regression method. The optimal orders of Chebyshev interpolation polynomial for channel tracking are found through computer simulations for LASMAX system. The simulation results show that the performance is significantly improved with channel tracking by employing Chebyshev interpolation polynomial at the expense of little increase of computation complexity.

articleTitle: A novel method for RCN s-t reliability analysis based on multipoint Pade approximation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Computing the reliability of a radio-communication network (RCN) is computationally difficult, and an exact solution is unattainable for many problems. Faced with this computational difficulty, we propose a novel approximant method to perform the s-t reliability analysis of RCN based on multipoint Pade approximant theory. We model the RCN by a probabilistic graph with reliable edges and unreliable nodes. An appropriate transformation is obtained using the recursive decomposition algorithm. And then the algorithm for s-t reliability analysis of RCN is presented using Werner algorithm. The efficiency of the method is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: An enhanced reactive dynamic source routing algorithm applied to mobile ad hoc networks
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Even though the reactive dynamic source routing protocol (RDSR) has been shown via simulations to be mostly efficient among all the existed routing protocols, it increases transmission delay. To overcome the above drawback in the reactive ad hoc routing protocol, this paper proposes an enhanced reactive ad hoc network routing protocol: ERDSR (enhanced reactive dynamic source routing protocol). ERDSR chooses the route by using the bandwidth and the number of hops of the available paths, and regulates the value of send/spl I.bar/timeout dynamically. Compared with RDSR by using ns-2 under various environments, ERDSR reduces the transmission delay and the average path length, and significantly improves the packet delivery ratio.

articleTitle: The UWB multiuser receivers with low complexity using turbo processing method
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: In this paper, we provide a joint optimized method for carrier-less UWB receivers based on the turbo principle. With this method, the sample rate of the receiving signal can be greatly reduced and the complexity of data processing is low for certain bit error rate. The simulation results show that good receiving performance can be obtained even less percentage of the multipath energy captured.

articleTitle: Deprived code division generalized processor sharing (DCDGPS) fair scheduler for WCDMA
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Scheduling algorithm plays an important role in the high rate service of WCDMA and future wireless. In this paper, a deprived code division generalized processor sharing fair scheduler (DCDGPS) is proposed for WCDMA system. The key of the algorithm is that traffic rate allows to dynamical adjusting according to the weight and traffic load. In some cases, the most urgent data may deprive other non-urgent data transmission channels which also transmit data at the same time, in order not to lost data. Simulation results show that the DCDGPS is effective scheme in comparison with other previously proposed scheduling algorithms, since it considers the fair of the packet loss.

articleTitle: Prototype development of venture capital project evaluation decision support system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: This paper develops the system prototype of venture capital project evaluation decision support system (VCPEDSS) by referring to project evaluation decision procedures of venture capital agencies.

articleTitle: Transient response analysis of interconnects in integrated circuit for wireless communications
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: A novel approach for transient analysis of coupled transmission line integrated circuits based on the generalized inverse matrix Pade approximation to exponential function (GIMPAe) is presented. Both transient response on the ends of the transmission line and along the transmission lines are given. The numerical result proved the efficient of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Channel estimation of uplink for MC-CDMA systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: Multi-carrier code division multiple access system (MC-CDMA) is a flexible and adaptable radio interface to provide dynamically changing bit rates and a variety of services on radio channels. An accurate channel estimate allows the use of multi-user detection and power loading to improve system performance. In this paper, we propose a novel channel estimation method of uplink for MC-CDMA systems. In MC-CDMA systems, code-multiplexed pilot symbols are transmitted consecutively in both time and frequency domains. In the proposed method, weighted pilot symbols in both domains are coherently added to improve signal to noise ratio of pilot symbols in channel estimation. We propose a method to select the weighting factor for pilot symbols according to the changes of propagation by measuring the maximum Doppler shift and the maximum delay time. Also the channel estimation algorithm is simplified. The method is evaluated in the end. The results show that the method is simple and effective.

articleTitle: Modified variable-order linear prediction speech modeling
publicationTitle: Proceedings. 2005 International Conference on Wireless Communications, Networking and Mobile Computing, 2005.
abstract: The variable-order filter method is used in linear prediction (LP) speech modeling. Since the prediction order would be very small for some frames in the method, it can reduce bit rate further. However, due to the large dynamic range of the speech spectrum it might happen that LP analysis is unable to match the higher formants properly if the prediction order is too small.
